verdict.rationale: Letta has its own shared-memory capability: Git-backed shared memory repositories, created via `letta shared-memory create`, give multiple agents the same files and context, while each agent keeps its own long-term memory. On the team side, teammates' agents and conversations are private by default, with org-level sharing controls. However, the evidence does not show shared memory repos being granted to other users, or per-repo permissions keeping particular memory private. missing for 10: documented user/team-level access controls on shared memory repositories, explicit selective sharing versus private memory scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can share selected memory across multiple agents or users (team or group memory) while keeping private memory private

citations.quote: Shared memory gives multiple agents access to the same files and working context. Each shared memory repository is a Git repository hosted in Letta Cloud
Each agent has its own identity and long-term memory
Membership lets teammates use the same organization while keeping each person's agents and conversations private by default.
Letta combines organization roles with sharing controls so teammates can collaborate without making all agent activity visible to the entire organization.
